the epoch mask hid the UNIT as well as the wall clock, so changing the divisor from nanoseconds-to-seconds to nanoseconds-to-milliseconds survived the entire suite
pyStrKey lost its number arm to the decoder swap: its only call site reads an ordered row so numbers arrive as json.Number, an arm it did not have, falling to a default of empty string
pyStrValue's json.Number arm returned the source literal, so "1.50" stayed 1.50 against CPython's 1.5, a content-key mismatch and a missed dedup
the content-key coercion test could not see any of it because its rows were Go literals rather than values that came through the decoder
the timestamp mask also hid the UTC offset, so dropping the .UTC() call survived the suite
the join test tested the helpers, not the site: swapping the two join helpers at the one line that needs the asymmetry survived everything
a doc comment cited a Python line that does not exist, in a file whose discipline is quoting the line being ported
SaveSuggestions was the one store-read site still dropping the announcement its own comment said tells an operator the corpus went short

the r1 depth fix bounded the depth of any token rather than open containers, so a nesting chain at exactly the limit was admitted by one reader and refused by the other; the r1 corpus had picked the boundary's neighbours
SaveSuggestions' dedup scan re-implemented the announced reader with different strip, split and bucket rules, and the author's own r1 comment in the same file had already named the site
changeLogAppend took a map type, so a nil map is a typed nil that matches FromPlain's map case and renders {} where CPython writes null
four findings were pasted-forward comments that no longer described their own site, including a copy count that was wrong and a paragraph describing a class the file is not in
SKILL_REWRITE reached the audience census as an undeclared event the moment rewrite.go landed; its lane was read off Python's live frozenset rather than inferred from neighbours

extract_json returns an empty dict on a parse failure, not None, so a garbled reply FAILS validation and goes to the repair loop; mapping Go's error to fail-open would promote every skill whose validation the model fumbled
stripRewriteFence's own strip was a dead second copy because the caller already strips; two fixtures written specifically to pin it both passed with the strip reverted

the harness test compared adapter calls by their purpose string, which is blind to the loop's whole point: dropping the rewrite's return value and re-validating the original produces identical purposes, count and promoted ids

the unjudged validation arm had no fixture because reaching it requires the validation call itself to fail mid-sweep; a raise sentinel in the probe script makes the failure happen on the call it means

pyIterate had arms for []any and string and none for []string, so a reply omitting steps_template raised in Go and rewrote the skill fine in Python: the third spelling of 'list', found by the third caller

three of the first run's eight failures were faults in the battery: an equivalent threshold mutant, a save call that rewrites the file to the same bytes, and a site-fail where the target had moved to a file the battery's list did not cover
three real fixture gaps were all masked the same way: the discriminating value was never the one that mattered (an outranked peer, a universally absent field, a trigger count below both thresholds)
fixing four decayed comments broke the timestamp census because it regexed raw bytes and read a prose sentence as a tenth offender; it now blanks comment spans, and the silent direction is worse
set_current_run_dir('') does not clear where None does because Path('') is the current directory, so one Go string cannot hold both answers and the stored value became a pointer
current_handle_id's split yields an EMPTY handle id, not an absent one, so folding empty into 'no run pinned' would make a caller resume the wrong run
max(0.0, float(v or 0)) is four coercions and none are decorative; the Go gate is spelled as a negated greater-than so NaN lands in the disabled arm rather than silently disabling pruning

Path.glob returns directories and unlink() on one raises IsADirectoryError which the except swallows, while Go's os.Remove SUCCEEDS on an empty directory, so without an IsDir skip the port would delete it and count it
_step_evidence renders the step number from a STORED one-based plan-item index; Go's StepOutcome had no such field and the slice position already disagrees in unported lanes
the strip is on the JOINED string, so a step with a result and no text keeps the space after the bracket; stripping the parts then joining produces neither spelling
_step_evidence's two keyword defaults mean 'the budget's own default' and zero is a real value a caller could pass, so a single Go signature makes zero ambiguous exactly where Python is unambiguous

the differential built its outcomes as literals, so zeroing the index assignment and making it zero-based both passed: the test pinned how the number renders and said nothing about where it comes from
the pruning differential entered through a local test helper that re-checked the empty-project condition before delegating, so the mutant deleting the production check passed
the artifact-dir test gave Python and Go the same root, so Python ran first and created the directory and the Go existence assertion passed whether or not ArtifactDir created anything

a (float64, bool) return separated 'float() would have raised' from 'the value was falsy', but every failing arm returns zero so the bool was implied by the caller's own gate; the answer was deleting it
the hex screen's fixture used a value BOTH runtimes reject; only a hex float with an exponent separates them
dropping the loop- prefix requirement survived because the fixture meant to catch it has no dash before its step token either way
the age comparison's strict-versus-inclusive bound is unobservable by construction because each runtime reads its own clock after the fixture's mtimes are set
drain_deferred_maintenance returns the callable count after a loop that swallows every exception, so a port that counted successes would agree on every fixture anyone writes first
the recover() has to be per-callable: one around the loop abandons the remaining callables where Python runs every one
the first version of the test HUNG rather than failed, the battery timed out at ten minutes, and the timeout killed the script before its restore step, leaving the mutant on disk
three mutants were rewritten for being equivalent: two computed a count and returned the length anyway, and one added an outer recover while keeping the inner ones
the evolver had grown FOUR private re-implementations of the shared str() family and three of the four were wrong in a way the shared one is not

the mint's stringDefault substituted the default when the value was missing OR EMPTY, which is `or` not .get, so five of five fields differed on one ordinary model reply and three of them are the inputs to the content key

str(raw.get('pattern','') or '') is a truthiness gate and a str(), but the port asserted a string type, so a guardrail whose pattern the model answered as a list reached the store empty, recorded as applied and matching nothing
an unordered map whose numbers are all float64 cannot answer the mint's questions at all: Repr refuses it and an integer suggestion reads back with a decimal point

CPython's Suggestion dataclass does not enforce its annotations, so a non-string suggestion stores the int and json.dumps writes it bare where Go's string field quotes it; pinned rather than fixed across 38 call sites
_content_key returns a 3-tuple and the port joined the three fields on U+0000, which a value containing that byte can confuse
a content-hash restamp mutant was correctly identified as equivalent because the hash does not cover the field the mutant changed

load_outcomes is TWO readers stacked and the port had only the first: on a store whose rows lack outcome_id and lessons, CPython loads nothing and the evolver skips the cycle while the port loaded them and minted suggestions off them

the exclusion filter already existed one layer too low, in the MEMORY.md renderer, with the reasoning 'the loader's tolerance is right for its other consumers' written down, and that reasoning was wrong
turning the outcome filter on failed twelve existing tests across five packages because every outcome seeder in the port produced rows the Python runtime reads as empty
routing the read through the announced reader made every number a json.Number and the int helper's float64 arm stopped matching, so MEMORY.md rendered 'Total tokens: 0' for a run with real usage
load_outcomes with a limit of zero returns nothing in CPython while the port reads a non-positive limit as everything; pinned as a named divergence

the sibling reader had the same missing half, and get_suggestion is the lookup the auto-revert guard uses, so a zero-filled answer hands that guard applied_manually=false, permission to revert a row a human applied
the suggestion filter failed a further fourteen tests across four packages, two of them tests of the lookup asserting against rows CPython answers as absent

two survivors were fixtures that cannot tell two answers apart: every non-string in the known-gap pin was a number, and both drifted rows were missing the same field set so the two drift messages were byte-identical
one mutant was written while the battery held a snapshot of the file it edited, so restoring between mutants reverted work done in parallel
te.get('is_error') is truthiness, not an identity test, so a stamp of the string 'no' is truthy in Python and a port reading it through a bool assertion calls that transcript clean
{name!r} and str(name) cannot share a helper: repr(None) and str(None) agree while repr and str of a string do not
the two clips are RUNE slices and this package deliberately did not become the seventh private clipRunes copy
the signature list is a TUPLE and next() takes the first MEMBER that matches, not the earliest match in the text, so a port scanning for the earliest offset reports a different string to the operator
FAILURE_CLASSES' descriptions are not documentation: diagnose_loop assigns the recommendation from that table, so the prose is a field on a persisted row
deleting the is_error check from the hallucination scan survived because every fixture carrying the marker phrase also carried is_error: true
a nil-versus-empty normalization with a comment defending it was the only reason a mutant survived, and json.dumps([]) is "[]" while a nil Go slice marshals to null into the shared events store
aliasing worstNames to the live streak is unkillable on its own because the reset branch nils the alias; the plausible port is the PAIR and only the pair is observable

COST_BY_MODEL is three naming systems for the same models and a key mistyped in the port does not fail, it falls through to the cheapest default; the differential sweeps every key in the CPython table

the arithmetic is spelled in Python's own term order because float addition is not associative and the result is compared against named dollar thresholds; the test compares seventeen significant digits, not a tolerance

RE2's \b is ASCII-only while Python's \w for a str pattern is str.isalnum() plus underscore, so an accented word has a boundary in Go and none in Python: two answers about the same step in a shared store
Python's \s matches the four information separators, NBSP, U+2007 and U+3000 (exactly str.isspace()) where Go's unicode.IsSpace omits the separators

the survivor: the two clamps in max(0, min(cache_read_tokens, tokens_in)) COMMUTE for every non-negative input, so swapping them is invisible to any fixture built from plausible inputs; the fixture now pins the order
three of 37 mutants failed to compile: a mutant that leaves an identifier unused is a fault in the battery, not a survivor
subprocess liveness and stall detection is unported: only the wall-clock timeout exists where Python also watches mtime and CPU
cost_usd estimation is unported, so rows omit the field rather than lie with a zero

config.Get cannot distinguish absent from explicit-null; config.Lookup is the presence half and callers feeding a coercing constructor must use it because float(None) raises where an absent key yields the default
Result.Warnings reach the operator via stderr only, and the comments now claim exactly that much and no more
jsonx with no fence present still takes the first balanced bracket in prose, shared verbatim with Python; fixing it is a cross-runtime change
